strategy.summary: createBookings() (src/bookings.ts) validates bookings (room, owner, half-hour UTC start, 30–240 min in 30-min steps), refuses same-room overlaps, lists a room's bookings by start time and lets only the owner cancel. Unit tests with Vitest against the real code and memoryStore() prove each rule and its refusal, asserting BookingError and the reason it gives.
inScope: book(): room, owner, start and length validation
Overlap rules per room, including touching bookings
cancel(): owner-only, freeing the slot, unknown id
outOfScope: The app's database-backed BookingStore (not in the repo); tests use memoryStore() as the README says
assumptions: memoryStore() is the store the tests use, as README.md says; no fakes are written.
The reason a booking is refused is shown by the BookingError message from src/bookings.ts (the only thing distinguishing refusals), so tests assert the exact message.
Owner names are matched after trimming whitespace, as the code does; matching is case-sensitive.
The at('HH:MM') builder moves to test/support/time.ts and is shared by both spec files.

risks.description: Off-by-one in overlap check could refuse back-to-back bookings or allow partial overlaps
risks.mitigation: TC8 covers each overlap shape; TC10 covers touching bookings in both directions

risks.description: Length/start boundaries (30, 240, non-multiples, sub-minute offsets) mis-validated
risks.mitigation: TC4–TC7 test both sides of each boundary

risks.description: Someone other than the owner cancels a booking
risks.mitigation: TC12 asserts refusal and that the booking stays listed

acceptanceCriteria.text: A booking names one of Atlas, Borealis, Cosmos and a non-blank owner, starts on the hour or half hour UTC and lasts 30–240 minutes in 30-minute steps; anything else is rejected with a BookingError saying why.
A booking overlapping another of the same room is rejected; different rooms never clash; a booking may start exactly when another ends.
A room's bookings are listed by start time.
Only the person who made a booking can cancel it, and cancelling frees its time.

review.standard: Working on the tests: keep every assertion the accepted strategy describes; Unit testing standards: assert the observable outcome
review.summary: TC10 only checks that the first booking is still listed (`toContainEqual(first)`), not that the touching booking was stored, although the accepted strategy expects both to be listed.
review.failureScenario: If `book()` returned the touching 12:00–13:00 (or 09:00–10:00) booking without saving it, e.g. a regression where `store.add` runs only when there are no other bookings in the room, `list('Atlas')` would return `[first]`. `toContainEqual(first)` still passes, so TC10 stays green even though the room never holds both back-to-back bookings. Asserting `expect(await bookings.list('Atlas')).toStrictEqual(<both, in start order>)` would catch it, as TC9 does for Borealis.
